answer: Each agent must solve a memory-hard puzzle tied to its own key every dawn, and the puzzle needs about 2 GB of RAM held for ten minutes. If any key misses a day, peers stop routing jobs to it. A farm can't share one solution, because each puzzle is seeded with that agent's key and the day's beacon. Running 500 fakes means 500 GB of RAM tied up every morning, so the cost grows with every fake. When our wharf cargo-audit agents and karst sensor agents checked rented servers, they found bulk memory got more expensive per gigabyte past one box.
